##: Xijing (戏鲸), the Pia戏 voice role-play client of aipiaxi.com.

The download page (aipiaxi.com/download) publishes a moving alias (.../app/pc/release.exe); this manifest uses the versioned installer from the vendor's own update feed (.../app/pc-new/windows/stable/latest.json), whose installerUrl points at .../windows/stable/Xijing-Setup-<version>.exe. Older versioned files stay online, so a recorded hash keeps working.

That feed is served with 'Cache-Control: max-age=31536000', which is why the site appends a per-request '?timestamp=' query. checkver therefore uses a script that appends its own timestamp instead of a plain jsonpath read, which could return a year-old edge copy.

autoupdate.hash is omitted for the same reason: Scoop cannot reproduce the cache-busting query, so the SHA-256 is recomputed by re-downloading the 90 MiB installer instead of trusting a possibly stale feed.

The NSIS installer is a plain payload (no embedded app-*.7z): the Flutter app already sits at the archive root with Xijing.exe, its plugin DLLs and data\ beside it. Only $PLUGINSDIR and Uninstall.exe are dropped.
Xijing.exe imports msvcp140.dll/vcruntime140.dll and the installer ships VcRedistInstaller.exe instead of the runtime itself, so the 2015-2022 redistributable is a declared dependency.
description: Voice role-play (Pia戏) and dubbing community client (戏鲸)
notes: The NSIS stubs ($PLUGINSDIR with WebView2Installer.exe and VcRedistInstaller.exe, Uninstall.exe) are dropped, so Scoop owns the uninstall.
User data, cache and logs are written under %APPDATA% and %LOCALAPPDATA%, so nothing needs to be persisted.
The bundled updater stays enabled and may prompt to update outside Scoop; run 'scoop install xijing -f' to return to the packaged build.
